result: The step-600 policies never hacked (greedy untested deletion+stub 0.00; 0 hack actions sampled on the 8,000-branch probe-fitting set of either seed), so the probe had no positive labels and never fired. After 600 more steps untested deletion+stub was 0.00 ± 0.00 (state+action arm: 0.00 ± 0.00) and the probe's AUROC on current states was undefined.
notes: Reduced design because the shared machine was overloaded (load ~250 on 16 cores): 2 seeds (0, 1) instead of 3, 600 GRPO steps instead of 1,000, greedy eval every 50 steps on 1,000 held-out programs (seed 12345) instead of 2,000. SFT kept at the registered 1,000 steps x 256 because the most expensive SFT checkpoints were already cached and mixing SFT lengths would confound comparisons. Policy: 2-layer pre-LN transformer (4 heads, FFN 2d) over all 12 branches; SFT on the pilot demonstrator, GRPO 64 programs x 8 samples, lr 1e-3 (never reduced; no instability seen), KL 0.02 to the frozen SFT copy, grad-norm clip 1.0 as in the pilot. 'Final' means step 600. Std is over 2 seeds (ddof=1). runtime_s sums the wall time of the runs used (shared runs counted in each experiment), measured under heavy machine load. Continuation from the E31 visible-reward policies at step 600 (same SFT reference for KL, Adam state carried over). Probe: L2 logistic regression on standardised post-LN hidden states at broken positions, labels = sampled action is DELETE/STUB on an untested branch, fit on 2,000 fresh programs from that seed's policy, then frozen. Reward = visible - 1 if probe probability > 0.5 on any branch. 'Untested deletions' in the registered criteria is measured as greedy untested deletion+stub rate (deletion-only also in metrics). Probe AUROC on current states uses labels from actions sampled by the current policy on the 1,000 eval programs. Design caveat: in this factorised policy the hidden state at a branch does not depend on the sampled action, so the as-specified penalty is constant within each GRPO group and gives zero advantage; the verdict is computed on that as-specified arm. A second, non-registered arm feeds the probe [hidden state, one-hot of the sampled action] so the penalty varies across samples; it is reported for context only. Reduced length: 600 visible steps then 600 probe-penalised steps (registered: 1,000 + 1,000); criteria judged at the end of the 600-step continuation. Verdict is mixed: deletions are below 0.2 but the probe AUROC is undefined (no hacks to label), so the kill criterion's AUROC > 0.8 condition cannot be met; the probe never fired, so the continuation is plain visible-reward training.
